arxiv-2303-06904.title: Contextually-rich human affect perception using multimodal scene information
arxiv-2303-06904.creator: Digbalay Bose, Rajat Hebbar, Krishna Somandepalli, Shrikanth Narayanan
arxiv-2303-06904.description: Abstract The process of human affect understanding involves the ability to infer person specific emotional states from various sources including images, speech, and language. Affect perception from images has predominantly focused on expressions extracted from salient face crops. However, emotions perceived by humans rely on multiple contextual cues including social settings, foreground interactions, and ambient visual scenes.

arxiv-2306-10696.title: On the functional equations of Siegel Eisenstein series of an odd prime level p p
arxiv-2306-10696.creator: Keiichi Gunji
arxiv-2306-10696.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Keiichi Gunji. Let p p be an odd prime. In this paper we write down the functional equations of Siegel Eisenstein series of degree n n , level p p with quadratic or trivial characters. First we study the U ⁡ ( p ) U(p) action in the space of Siegel Eisenstein series to get U ⁡ ( p ) U(p) -eigen functions.

arxiv-2310-00906.title: A Decentralized Cooperative Navigation Approach for Visual Homing Networks
arxiv-2310-00906.creator: Mohamed Rahouti, Damian Lyons, Senthil Kumar Jagatheesaperumal, and Kaiqi Xiong
arxiv-2310-00906.description: Abstract Visual homing is a lightweight approach to visual navigation. Given the stored information of an initial ‘home’ location, the navigation task back to this location is achieved from any other location by comparing the stored home information to the current image and extracting a motion vector.

arxiv-2407-11983.title: Generative AI as a Learning Buddy and Teaching Assistant: Pre-service Teachers’ Uses and Attitudes
arxiv-2407-11983.creator: Matthew Nyaaba, Lehong Shi, Macharious Nabang, Xiaoming Zhai, Patrick Kyeremeh, Samuel Arthur Ayoberd, Bismark Nyaaba Akanzire
arxiv-2407-11983.description: Abstract To uncover pre-service teachers’ (PSTs’) user experience and perceptions of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) applications, we surveyed 167 Ghana PSTs’ specific uses of GenAI as the learning buddy and teaching assistant and their attitudes towards these applications. Employing exploratory factor analysis (EFA), we identified three key factors shaping PSTs’ attitudes toward GenAI, teaching, learning, and ethical and advocacy factors.

arxiv-2503-16428.title: XAttention: Block Sparse Attention with Antidiagonal Scoring
arxiv-2503-16428.creator: Ruyi Xu, Guangxuan Xiao, Haofeng Huang, Junxian Guo, Song Han
arxiv-2503-16428.description: Abstract Long-Context Transformer Models (LCTMs) are vital for real-world applications but suffer high computational costs due to attention’s quadratic complexity. Block-sparse attention mitigates this by focusing computation on critical regions, yet existing methods struggle with balancing accuracy and efficiency due to costly block importance measurements.

arxiv-2505-00191.title: IP-CRR: Information Pursuit for Interpretable Classification of Chest Radiology Reports
arxiv-2505-00191.creator: Yuyan Ge, Kwan Ho Ryan Chan, Pablo Messina, René Vidal
arxiv-2505-00191.description: Abstract The development of AI-based methods for analyzing radiology reports could lead to significant advances in medical diagnosis—from improving diagnostic accuracy to enhancing efficiency and reducing workload. However, the lack of interpretability in these methods has hindered their adoption in clinical settings. In this paper, we propose an interpretable-by-design framework for classifying radiology reports.

arxiv-2509-04630.title: Quasi-continuum approximations for nonlinear dispersive waves in general discrete conservation laws
arxiv-2509-04630.creator: Su Yang
arxiv-2509-04630.description: Abstract In this paper, we study a non-integrable discrete lattice model which is a variant of an integrable discretization of the standard Hopf equation. Interestingly, a direct numerical simulation of the Riemann problem associated with such a discrete lattice shows the emergence of both the dispersive shock wave (DSW) and rarefaction wave (RW).

arxiv-2601-11330.title: Search for dark matter produced in association with a Higgs boson decaying to bottom quarks in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2601-11330.description: Abstract A search for dark matter particles produced in association with a Higgs boson decaying to a bottom quark-antiquark pair in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV is presented. The data, collected with the CMS detector at the LHC, correspond to an integrated luminosity of 101 \fbinv .

arxiv-2602-14451.creator: Qianyue Wang Jinwu Hu Huanxiang Lin Bolin Chen, Zhiquan Wen Yaofo Chen Yu Rong Mingkui Tan
arxiv-2602-14451.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Qianyue Wang Jinwu Hu Huanxiang Lin Bolin Chen, Zhiquan Wen Yaofo Chen Yu Rong Mingkui Tan. pmc-10492488.title: Association of Psychological Readiness to Return to Sports With Subjective Level of Return at 12 Months After ACL Reconstruction
pmc-10492488.creator: Makoto Suzuki, Tomoya Ishida, Hisashi Matsumoto, Satoru Kaneko, Chiharu Inoue, Yoshimitsu Aoki, Harukazu Tohyama, Mina Samukawa
pmc-10492488.description: Background:Return-to-sports (RTS) rates after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction (ACLR) differ according to the level at which patients return. It is unclear whether the level of RTS is affected by psychological readiness to return.Purpose:To examine the association between psychological readiness to RTS and subjective RTS level 12 months after ACLR.Study Design:Case-control study; Level of evidence, 3.

pmc-11409276.title: Geriatric psychiatry and brain health in old age
pmc-11409276.creator: Rajesh R Tampi, Jordan F Karp
pmc-11409276.description: ese disorders account for 10.6% of the total years lived with disability for this age group. 2 Common neuropsychiatric disorders among older adults include anxiety disorders, mood disorders, substance use disorders, neurocognitive disorders, especially due to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), and delirium.3,4 Despite being common and causing significant difficulties, psychiatric disorders are often undiagnosed and untreated in late life.

pmc-11433703.title: Thermo-Responsive Hydrogel Based on Lung Decellularized Extracellular Matrix for 3D Culture Model to Enhance Cancer Stem Cell Characteristics
pmc-11433703.creator: Lei Chen, Fanglu Li, Ruobing Li, Ke Zheng, Xinyi Zhang, Huijing Ma, Kaiming Li, Lei Nie, Carmelo Corsaro
pmc-11433703.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are most likely the main cause of lung cancer formation, metastasis, drug resistance, and genetic heterogeneity. Three-dimensional (3D) ex vivo cell culture models can facilitate stemness improvement and CSC enrichment. Considering the critical role of extracellular matrix (ECM) on CSC properties, the present study developed a thermo-responsive hydrogel using the porcine decellularized lung for 3D cell culture, and the cell-laden hydrogel culturing model was used to explore the CSC characteristics and potential utilization in CSC-specific drug evaluation.

pmc-11476814.title: Why does malaria transmission continue at high levels despite universal vector control? Quantifying persistent malaria transmission by Anopheles funestus in Western Province, Zambia
pmc-11476814.creator: Ruth A Ashton, Benjamin Chanda, Chama Chishya, Rayford Muyabe, Tresford Kaniki, Patricia Mambo, Mwansa Mwenya, Gift Mwaanga, Annie Arnzen, Erica Orange, Kochelani Saili, Handrinah Banda Yikona, John Chulu, Chanda Chitoshi, Irene Kyomuhangi, John Miller, Kafula Silumbe, Busiku Hamainza, Megan Littrel
pmc-11476814.description: BackgroundSome settings continue to experience a high malaria burden despite scale-up of malaria vector control to high levels of coverage. Characterisation of persistent malaria transmission in the presence of standard control measures, also termed residual malaria transmission, to understand where and when individuals are exposed to vector biting is critical to inform refinement of prevention and control strategies.

pmc-11644215.title: Electrical Bioimpedance-Based Monitoring of Intracochlear Tissue Changes After Cochlear Implantation
pmc-11644215.creator: Leanne Sijgers, Marlies Geys, Gunnar Geissler, Patrick Boyle, Alexander Huber, Flurin Pfiffner, Mart Min
pmc-11644215.description: Background: This study examined electrical bioimpedance as a biomarker for intracochlear tissue changes after cochlear implant surgery, comparing monopolar, three-point, and four-point impedance measurements over time and evaluating different measurement systems and approaches. Methods: Impedance measurements were obtained from 21 participants during surgery and at four postoperative stages.

pmc-12743104.title: The cell death regulator c-FLIPR impairs natural killer cell responses during influenza a virus infection
pmc-12743104.creator: André Carmo-Fernandes, Neda Tafrishi, Clara Bessen, Konstantinos Katsoulis-Dimitriou, Marina C. Greweling-Pils, Dunja Bruder, Carlos Plaza-Sirvent, Ingo Schmitz
pmc-12743104.description: Apoptosis, a form of programmed cell death, is crucial for keeping homeostasis during and after infections. Cellular FLICE-inhibitory protein (c-FLIP) is an inhibitor of death receptor-mediated apoptosis, of which three isoforms have been characterized so far. While the isoforms c-FLIPlong and c-FLIPshort are well characterized, the function of c-FLIPR remains poorly understood.

pmc-13049524.title: Impact of trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) and brain stereotactic radiosurgery on intracranial control and radionecrosis risk in HER2-positive or -low breast cancer brain metastases
pmc-13049524.creator: Seok-Joo Chun, Kyubo Kim, Won Ick Chang, Yong Bae Kim, Sun Ha Paek, Kyung-Hun Lee, Jin-Ho Song, Ji Hyun Hong, Jieun Lee, Won Il Jang, Tae Hyun Kim, Kyung Hwan Shin
pmc-13049524.description: BackgroundWhile trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) demonstrates intracranial efficacy, the potential for radionecrosis (RN) when combined with stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) remains a concern, given the established risk with other antibody-drug conjugates like T-DM1. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of T-DXd and SRS in patients with HER2-positive or -low breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM).

pmc-13575487.title: Facial Nerve Hemangioma in the Internal Auditory Canal: A Rare Localization and Therapeutic Challenge
pmc-13575487.creator: Yasmine Elamrani, Mohammed-Amine Salek, Achraf Amine Sbai, Drissia Benfadil, Azzedine Lachkar, Fahd El Ayoubi El Idrissi
pmc-13575487.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveFacial nerve hemangiomas (FNHs) are rare vascular tumors that often mimic other facial nerve disorders, making diagnosis and management challenging. This report highlights a case of FNH in the internal auditory canal (IAC) successfully treated via a translabyrinthine approach.Case PresentationA 64‐year‐old female patient with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue presented with progressive left‐sided peripheral facial paralysis (House–Brackmann Grade IV), associated with ipsilateral hearing loss and vertigo.

pmc-13659930.title: Efficacy and Safety of Enlicitide in Hypercholesterolemia: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-13659930.creator: Muhammad Farhan, Muhammad Murtaza, Muhammad Mujtaba Rasool, Farah Khan, Hammad Amjad, Kuldeep Dalpat Rai, Sheikh Muhammad Ebtehaj Ali, Ahmed Asad Raza, Muhammad Ahmad Sohail, Abedin Samadi, Furqan Hassan
pmc-13659930.description: BackgroundAtherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low‐density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL‐C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high‐risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL‐C targets. Enlicitide (MK‐0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9‐directed therapies.

uslaw-usc-t18-s1707.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1707 — Theft of property used by Postal Service
uslaw-usc-t18-s1707.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s1707.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 83 (Postal Service). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever steals, purloins, or embezzles any property used by the Postal Service, or appropriates any such property to his own or any other than its proper use, or conveys away any such property to the hindrance or detriment of the public.
